previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with HCV-related cirrhosis, hepatocellular carcinoma, and a history of TIPS placement, was admitted due to coffee ground emesis and melena concerning for an upper gastrointestinal bleed. His hemoglobin was 6.2 g/dL on presentation, and he received three units of packed red blood cells. An EGD revealed an esophageal ulcer and portal hypertensive gastropathy without active bleeding. He underwent a large volume paracentesis with removal of 6 liters of fluid; microbiology showed no infection. His hyponatremia fluctuated but remained asymptomatic. He was managed with pantoprazole, octreotide, and continued home medications including lactulose and rifaximin. He remained stable, with no rebleeding, and was discharged home with plans for follow-up EGD in three months, hepatology follow-up, and monitoring for signs of recurrence.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  LIVER OR GALLBLADDER US (SINGLE ORGAN)

INDICATION:  ___ with hep c cirrhosis  // ? portal vein patency

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the abdomen were
obtained.

COMPARISON:  ___ liver ultrasound.
___ outside hospital CT abdomen.

FINDINGS: 

LIVER: The hepatic parenchyma is markedly coarsened and nodular in appearance.
Focal lesions/RFA beds are better assessed on prior cross-sectional imaging.

The spleen is enlarged, measuring 15.2 cm.  There is large volume ascites. 
There is no intrahepatic biliary dilation.  The gallbladder is full of
gallstones, which limits evaluation.  The CHD measures 3 mm. Evaluation of the
pancreas is limited by overlying bowel gas.

The main portal vein is patent with hepatopetal flow.
The TIPS is patent and demonstrates wall-to-wall flow.
Portal vein and intra-TIPS velocities are as follows:
Main portal vein:  33 cm/sec, previously 39 cm/sec
Proximal TIPS:  100 cm/sec, previously  84 cm/sec
Mid TIPS:  183 cm/sec, previously 226 cm/sec
Distal TIPS:  192 cm/sec, previously 170 cm/sec

Flow within the left portal vein is away from the TIPS shunt. Flow within the
right anterior and right posterior portal vein is  towards the TIPS.  Flow
within the recanalized paraumbilical vein is away from the TIPS.  Appropriate
flow is seen in the hepatic veins and IVC.

IMPRESSION:


1. No evidence of portal vein thrombosis.
2. Patent TIPS with wall-to-wall flow.  Velocities similar compared to prior.
3. New hepatopetal flow within the left hepatic portal vein away from the TIPS
likely draining via patent umbilical vein.
4. Splenomegaly and large volume ascites.

EXAMINATION:  Ultrasound-guided therapeutic and diagnostic paracentesis.

INDICATION:  ___ man with HCV cirrhosis with recurrent ascites  // LVP

TECHNIQUE:  Ultrasound guided diagnostic and therapeutic paracentesis

FINDINGS: 

Limited grayscale ultrasound imaging of the abdomen demonstrated a large
amount of ascites. A suitable target in the deepest pocket in the right lower
quadrant was selected for paracentesis.

PROCEDURE:  The procedure, risks, benefits and alternatives were discussed
with the patient and written informed consent was obtained.

A preprocedure time-out was performed discussing the planned procedure,
confirming the patient's identity with 3 identifiers, and reviewing a
checklist per ___ protocol.

Under ultrasound guidance, an entrance site was selected and the skin was
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion. 1% lidocaine was instilled
for local anesthesia.

A 5 ___ catheter was advanced into the largest fluid pocket in the right
lower quadrant and 6 L of clear, yellow/amber fluid was removed. Fluid samples
were submitted to the laboratory for cell count, differential, and culture.

The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate complication.
Estimated blood loss was minimal.

Dr. ___ personally supervised the trainee during the key components of
the procedure and reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful diagnostic and therapeutic ultrasound-guided
paracentesis (6L RLQ).
Hematology, chemistry, and microbiology samples were obtained and results are
pending.
